_comment: Reference snippet — NOT installed by ai-sync. Merge the permissions block into
your project's .claude/settings.json by hand.
Why: a subagent's `tools:` frontmatter is all-or-nothing per tool. It can grant or
withhold Bash, but it cannot express 'Bash, but only read commands'. The reviewing
role agents (qa, architect, product, engineering-manager, sre, senior-dev) need Bash
to run a test suite and read git metadata, so their read-only guarantee is otherwise
enforced only by instructions in the agent body. docs-sync needs the same fence for
the same reason, even though it can edit — its Bash is for reading git history to see
what changed, not for anything that mutates. These deny rules make all of that real.
The build/plan/deploy entries matter most for `sre`, which reads Dockerfiles, Terraform
and Kubernetes manifests: `terraform plan` downloads and executes provider plugins and
`docker build` runs the target repo's own tooling, so both are executing untrusted code
even though neither sounds like it mutates anything.
Scope caveat: permissions in settings.json apply to the WHOLE project, not per-agent.
These rules will also block you from running these commands in a normal session. If
your workflow needs any of them, drop that line rather than the whole block — and if
you routinely commit from inside Claude Code, this block is not for you.
ciso, planner, and tracker need no rules here: they are granted no Bash at all, which
is a harder guarantee than any deny list. developer and docs-sync are the two roles
meant to change the repo (code and documentation respectively) and both run only on
deliberate invocation — developer additionally requires named, human-approved items.
